utterances.text: I apologise. I had not understood that to be their suggestion but that's certainly acceptable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is that acceptable?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. In that event it looks like we have an adjourn now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm afraid so, Your Honour, because we don't have another witness available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I understand that. Okay. That will satisfy the Defence. That was the suggestion of the Defence. Am I right, Mr. Milovancevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I agree with your proposal. If I'm given the floor, let me just be brief and say this: I think that Mr. Whiting owes us another explanation. If they informed us in writing that the witness will testify about facts, viva voce, and that this witness gave a statement, then according to the Rules, the statement has to be disclosed to us. We were informed three or four days ago, that in addition to being an expert witness, this witness will also be a fact witness, testifying about some facts that witnesses from UNPROFOR and UNHCR were supposed to testify about. I just want to avoid any problems in that sense and this is what I'm pointing out to the Trial Chamber. I hope you understood me. I hope I was clear enough. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And I hope the Chamber understood you and I hope you understood Mr. Whiting when he said they have not taken a statement from this witness, that is why they have had nothing to turn over to the Defence. If they had taken a statement on the facts, they would have tendered that statement to you and he says this is standard practice. If it comes to you as a little addendum to an expert testimony that he also testifies on the facts so there was nothing according to Mr. Whiting to be turned over to the Defence. Okay?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Before we adjourn, then, one or two points on housekeeping. Yesterday -- I beg your pardon. On the 16th, on Monday, there was an arrangement that the parties work on the agreed facts reflecting the two corrections discussed on that day, on the 16th of January. The parties promised to do so. The Chamber would like to find out from the parties how far they've gone on that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have had discussions. I think it will be resolved very quickly and my understanding is that the Chamber expects us to file a new version of the agreed facts and we can certainly do that and have that done by next week. I don't see any difficulty whatsoever in having that done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I do not think it's necessarily a new version, it's just maybe to deal with throws two items and say whether you agree or disagree on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I misunderstood your legal counsel, then I thought he wanted us to file a new version. But we can do it that way if that's easier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I think it's easier and quicker and shorter.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I just want to make sure it doesn't go to the back burner and gets forgotten. That's why it will be raised now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I think there is just one little detail to discuss furthers with counsel. I don't see any difficulty in resolving it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Whiting. You confirm that, Mr. Milovancevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. The next point the Chamber would like to discuss is in terms of the new courtroom calendar distributed, we are supposed to sit on Friday, the 3rd of February, from 9.00 a.m. to 13.45 in this courtroom. Is that convenient for all parties? Mr. Whiting?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. That's fine, Your Honour. And then we're still sitting the next week, on the 6th and the 7th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That has not been removed.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the president, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, I think your microphone is off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Well, then, the Chamber will then sit in addition to the days that have already been allocated, we will also sit on the 3rd of February, from nine in the morning to quarter to two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I had forgotten ask my colleagues. In that event, that brings us to the end of the proceedings for today and the matter stands adjourned until next week, Thursday. In which court?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't have the courtroom number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is at 9.00 in the morning. Can somebody remind me to which court it is? Courtroom III, the same courtroom, and that will be at nine in the morning. Thank you very much. The court will adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 26th day of January, 2006, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 4.50 p.m.,
